subject: POC Observability Plan - success criteria & timeline
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Redwood POC - Observability discussion

Hi Marissa / Jordan,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the demo and the high-level discussion about how Redwood could help us with inference observability during our POC. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can align internal stakeholders: 

1) Primary success criteria (what we heard):
- Ability to see per-request latency breakdown (queue, model, network) and per-model token cost estimates
- End-to-end tracing that links incoming API request IDs to model inference traces and downstream logs
- Exportable metrics and logs for our SIEM and internal dashboards
- Alerts on error rates and latency regressions relative to baseline

2) POC scope we expect to run:
- 2-week active trial using a dedicated staging dataset and a single production-like route (~100 RPS burst testing)
- Compare performance and cost vs our current managed endpoint

Questions:
- Can Redwood provide a sample dashboard and a minimal tracing integration guide for our engineers?
- Who owns configuring alerts and exporting logs during the POC — Redwood or FintechX?

Next steps: if you can send the observability checklist and timeline we can schedule internal signoffs.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Engineering, FintechX
alex.johnson@fintechx.com


From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Hi Alex — great to chat earlier. Appreciate the clear success criteria.

Short answers to your questions:
- Yes — I attached our "observability-poc-checklist.xlsx" and a dashboard mockup. They cover the baseline dashboards we typically provision for POCs (latency waterfall, per-model throughput/cost, error rates, and trace sampling).
- Ownership: Redwood will ship the initial dashboard and tracing integration snippets. FintechX will have ownership for alert thresholds and exporting logs to your SIEM; we can help set up the export during the POC.

Proposed POC timeline (two-week active window):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, get staging credentials, enable tracing and log export (Redwood & FintechX infra lead)
- Week 1: Run baseline tests (no caching, baseline traffic), validate dashboards & traces
- Week 2: Performance/cost compare and regression checks; review success criteria with stakeholders

Success criteria (as plain acceptance items):
- Dashboard shows per-request latency waterfall and per-model token cost within 10% of observed production numbers
- Traces successfully tie request IDs to model inference spans with at least 90% coverage for sampled requests
- Logs export to FintechX SIEM (AWS Kinesis/CloudWatch or GCP Pub/Sub) and are queryable within 10 minutes
- No critical errors and an error rate <0.5% during baseline traffic window

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm staging credentials and who on your side will be the infra owner (name + email)
- Jordan/Sean: please review the checklist and flag anything we should add from the infra/engineering side

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a short kickoff once we have the infra owner.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Adding a few technical items for the checklist and what we'll provision during the POC: 

Telemetry & dashboards: 
- Latency waterfall (client queue, routing, model execution, serialization) per request ID
- Per-model and per-route token cost estimation (tokens * model unit cost) aggregated by minute
- Error classification dashboard (model errors vs infra vs client input) + sample request inspector

Tracing / logs: 
- We'll provide an OpenTelemetry collector configuration for your staging environment and a short snippet to inject request IDs into headers so traces are correlated end-to-end
- Default trace sampling at 5% with an option to increase to 20% during burst tests
- Log export options: CloudWatch LogGroup subscription or GCP Pub/Sub sink; we can also push to a secure S3 bucket if you prefer

Alerts & SLOs: 
- Baseline latency p50/p95 targets will be captured during Week 1 and we'll propose alert thresholds (e.g., p95 > 1.5x baseline for 5m)
- Error rate alerts for >0.5% over 5m and a model-specific spike alert (e.g., if a single model shows a >2x error rate increase)

Instrumentation ownership: Jordan/Redwood will provision the OTEL config and dashboards. FintechX infra will enable the collector and provide the sink details. We'll work together to set final thresholds.

If anyone on the FintechX side prefers a quick technical sync, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow.

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
